author: @fl0rianr

evidence.api_compatibility: No documented public API is affected — the reverted feature was never documented. The /internal/mcp/* admin routes from #2605 are removed; anyone who had begun using them will see those endpoints disappear (404). This is a breaking change for zero documented users, acknowledged by the author as an assumption rather than a certainty. The MCP gateway (POST /mcp, Mcp-Session-Id CORS header, docs/api/mcp.md) is untouched and unaffected.
evidence.documentation: No documentation changes needed — the feature was never documented. No existing docs reference the reverted endpoints or the mcp_client module. The MCP gateway docs at docs/api/mcp.md are unaffected.
evidence.manual_release_testing: This PR removes features rather than adding or changing them. There are no user-facing surfaces to exercise in this release. Residual risk: anyone who happened to use the undocumented /internal/mcp/* endpoints from a prior build containing #2605 will no longer have those routes — they will receive 404s. The PR author and reviewer considered this acceptable per the RFC decision, but a release note noting the removal of the previously undocumented MCP client endpoints would be prudent for user communication.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No post-approval commits. The PR has a single commit (49febe3) authored on 2026-09-03. Approval came on 2026-09-08 — six days later — with no intervening changes. The branch was clean from approval to merge.
evidence.review: PR #3498 was approved by @ramkrishna2910 (MEMBER) who stated 'Revert is clean. Built and tested locally.' (@ramkrishna2910's subject areas include MCP, per docs/dev/contribute.md). @jeremyfowers also engaged by asking Claude to verify revert completeness. The automated Claude review performed an exhaustive tree-wide search for residual references (mcp_client, mcp_servers, McpClient, MCPClient, internal/mcp, mock_mcp_stdio) and found zero hits. Two non-blocking notes were raised: (a) a stray mcp_servers.json file may travel during legacy cache migration, which is harmless; (b) byte-level diff against #2605 was not feasible, but exhaustive symbol search serves as a substitute.
evidence.security: Removing an internal process-launching endpoint from /internal/mcp/* improves the security posture: no one can register and run arbitrary MCP servers through Lemonade anymore. The pre-existing /internal/* routes remain gated behind admin_api_key_ as before. No new credential handling, network calls, or code execution paths are introduced.
evidence.tests: The test file test/cpp/test_mcp_client_config.cpp (320 lines) and test/fixtures/mock_mcp_stdio_server.py (129 lines) were deleted along with the feature. test/cpp/test_config_dir_migration.cpp was updated to remove references to mcp_servers.json from both the source migration array (path_utils.cpp, 5→4 entries) and the CMake test expectations. All CI checks passed: C++ build+test, Docker smoke, container builds (amd64+arm64), CodeQL, and routing schema tests all reported SUCCESS. Two unrelated test suites (mcp-client-integration and build-on-distro) were skipped, which is expected since the target code no longer exists.

subject: revert internal mcp client code (#3498)
summary: Reverts the internal MCP client agent and its admin-gated /internal/mcp/* endpoints introduced in PR #2605, restoring the pre-feature codebase state.
verdict_reason: This is a well-scoped, cleanly executed revert backed by a member's local build-and-test and a thorough automated verification that zero residual MCP-client references remain.
